Q0251

David Hume

A verified English rendering from the curated archive.

Quotes / David Hume / Q0251

English

Reason is wholly inactive, and can never be the source of so active a principle as conscience, or a sense of morals.
Thinker David Hume
School Moral Philosophy
Source Enquiry Concerning the Principles of Morals, App. I
Theme Morality
Another quotation More from this thinker

Context and commentary are editorial aids for reading. They do not replace the primary text or scholarly commentary.

Source context

This English passage is associated with Enquiry Concerning the Principles of Morals, App. I, within the tradition of Moral Philosophy. The wording below is a verified rendering prepared for careful reading rather than a claim of unique translation authority.

A short reading

Read in the register of morality, the sentence asks the reader to test an assumption rather than to collect a slogan. In David Hume's wider work, similar claims are usually offered as prompts for judgment: what would have to be true for the sentence to hold, and what would follow if it did?
